group.passage:
Today, millions of people put on glasses every morning without a second thought. For most of history, however, people whose eyesight weakened with age simply had to live with a blurry view of the world. As reading and sewing grew harder each year, many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.
Some readers laid a piece of polished crystal on the page to [[2]] the letters, making them look bigger. The first true eyeglasses appeared in northern Italy in the late 1200s, yet no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded. These early glasses had no arms, so users had to hold them up by hand or rest them on the nose. Because every lens was shaped by hand, glasses were so [[4]] at first that few ordinary people could afford them. Still, scholars and monks, who could now keep reading into old age, were full of [[5]] for the new invention.
After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[6]] for glasses rose sharply, and workshops began producing them in large numbers. Lenses for people who could not see distant objects came later. Early frames, however, were [[7]] to wear: they pinched the nose and slipped off at the slightest movement. It was not until the 1700s that side arms resting on the ears became common, so wearers no longer had to hold their glasses in place.
For centuries, glasses were also seen as a sign of weakness or old age, and many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public. Today, attitudes have changed completely. Glasses now come in all kinds of shapes and colors, and many people choose frames that [[9]] their face and personality. Some even wear glasses with plain lenses just because they like the look, turning a medical [[10]] into a fashion accessory.

tags.topic: how eyeglasses developed from hand-held lenses into a fashion accessory

1.explanation_zh: were forced to ___ their trades 需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades（他們的手藝、行業）。前一句說視力隨年紀退化、看出去一片模糊，本句又說閱讀和縫紉一年比一年難，所以許多技術工人被迫「放棄」手藝；long before they wished to（遠早於他們希望的時間）也說明這是不得已的。
evidence: As reading and sewing grew harder each year, many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward（形容詞，不方便的、不好用的；也常指「尷尬的」）詞性不合：空格在 were forced to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades。
option_notes_zh.B: device（名詞，裝置、器材）詞性不合：空格在 were forced to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify 是原形動詞，但 magnify their trades（放大他們的手藝）不通；magnify 屬於第 2 格。
option_notes_zh.D: praise 也可當動詞（讚美），但「被迫讚美自己的手藝」和「視力變差、工作越來越難」的因果不合；praise 在本文是第 5 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 were forced to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades。
option_notes_zh.G: demand 也可當動詞（要求），但 were forced to demand their trades 不通；demand 在本文是第 6 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit 是原形動詞，但 suit their trades（適合他們的手藝）語意不通，也和 forced、long before they wished to 的「不得已」不合；suit 屬於第 9 格。
option_notes_zh.I: credit 也可當動詞（歸功於），但 were forced to credit their trades 不通；credit 在本文是第 3 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive（形容詞，昂貴的）詞性不合：空格在 were forced to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 their trades。

1.strategy_zh: to 後面要原形動詞；從「視力變差、工作越來越難」和 forced、long before they wished to 推出工人只好「放棄」手藝。
hints: were forced to ___ their trades：to 後面要原形動詞。
視力越來越差，閱讀和縫紉越來越難，工人只好怎麼做？
答案是片語動詞，意思是「放棄」。

2.explanation_zh: to ___ the letters 是表目的的不定詞，需要原形及物動詞。把一片磨亮的水晶放在書頁上，是為了「放大」字母；逗號後的分詞片語 making them look bigger（讓字看起來更大）正好說明了這個字的意思。
evidence: Some readers laid a piece of polished crystal on the page to [[2]] the letters, making them look bigger.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward（形容詞，不方便的、不好用的；也常指「尷尬的」）詞性不合：空格在表目的的不定詞 to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the letters。
option_notes_zh.B: device（名詞，裝置、器材）詞性不合：空格在表目的的不定詞 to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the letters。
option_notes_zh.D: praise 也可當動詞，但 praise the letters（讚美字母）和 making them look bigger 不合；praise 在本文是第 5 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在表目的的不定詞 to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the letters。
option_notes_zh.F: give up the letters（放棄字母）和「把水晶放在書頁上讓字變大」的目的相反；give up 屬於第 1 格。
option_notes_zh.G: demand 也可當動詞，但 demand the letters（要求字母）不通；demand 在本文是第 6 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit the letters（適合字母）不通，也不能說明 making them look bigger；suit 屬於第 9 格。
option_notes_zh.I: credit 也可當動詞，但 credit the letters 不通；credit 在本文是第 3 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive（形容詞，昂貴的）詞性不合：空格在表目的的不定詞 to 之後，需要原形及物動詞，受詞是 the letters。

2.strategy_zh: to＋原形動詞表示目的；逗號後的 making them look bigger 就是答案的意思。
hints: to ___ the letters：to 後面要原形動詞。
看逗號後面：making them look bigger。
答案的意思是「放大」。

3.explanation_zh: take ___ for 需要名詞；take credit for（把……的功勞歸給自己、居功）是固定說法。because the maker’s name was never recorded（製作者的名字從未被記錄下來）說明為什麼沒有人能說發明眼鏡是自己的「功勞」。praise 和 credit 意思相近（讚揚），但英文不說 take praise for；praise 要用在第 5 格 be full of praise for。
evidence: The first true eyeglasses appeared in northern Italy in the late 1200s, yet no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward（形容詞，不方便的、不好用的；也常指「尷尬的」）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: take device for inventing them 不通；device 屬於第 10 格。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.D: praise（讚美）和 credit 意思相近，但 take praise for 不是英文的固定說法（只說 take credit for）；praise 屬於第 5 格 were full of praise for。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.F: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: take demand for 不是英文說法；demand 屬於第 6 格 the demand for glasses。
option_notes_zh.H: suit 也可當名詞（西裝），但 take suit for inventing them 不通；suit 在本文是第 9 格的動詞。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive（形容詞，昂貴的）詞性不合：空格在 take 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。

3.strategy_zh: 看到 take ___ for，想到固定說法 take credit for；because 子句說明沒人知道發明者是誰。
hints: take ___ for：需要名詞。
because the maker’s name was never recorded：沒人知道是誰發明的，所以沒有人能怎樣？
「把功勞歸給自己」英文說 take ___ for。

4.explanation_zh: glasses were so ___ at first that … 需要形容詞（so＋形容詞＋that 子句表示結果）。Because every lens was shaped by hand（每片鏡片都是手工磨製）說明原因，that 子句 few ordinary people could afford them（很少一般人買得起）說明結果，所以眼鏡起初非常「昂貴」。
evidence: Because every lens was shaped by hand, glasses were so [[4]] at first that few ordinary people could afford them.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward 是形容詞，但「戴起來不方便」和 could afford them（買得起）無關；手工製作、很少人買得起，說的是價錢。awkward 屬於第 7 格 awkward to wear。
option_notes_zh.B: device（名詞，裝置、器材）詞性不合：空格在 were so 之後、that 子句之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 were so 之後、that 子句之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.D: praise（名詞，讚美、稱讚（也可當動詞））詞性不合：空格在 were so 之後、that 子句之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed 是形容詞，但主詞是 glasses（眼鏡），物品不會「感到羞愧」，也和 could afford 無關；ashamed 屬於第 8 格。
option_notes_zh.F: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 were so 之後、that 子句之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.G: demand（名詞，需求（也可當動詞「要求」））詞性不合：空格在 were so 之後、that 子句之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit（動詞，適合（也可當名詞「西裝」））詞性不合：空格在 were so 之後、that 子句之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.I: credit（名詞，功勞、讚揚；take credit for＝居功）詞性不合：空格在 were so 之後、that 子句之前，需要形容詞。

4.strategy_zh: so ___ that 中間要形容詞；看 that 子句的 afford（買得起），答案和價錢有關。
hints: were so ___ at first that …：中間需要形容詞。
每片鏡片都要手工磨製，結果 few ordinary people could afford them。
答案的意思是「昂貴的」。

5.explanation_zh: were full of ___ for 需要名詞；be full of praise for（對……讚不絕口）是常見搭配。學者和修士 could now keep reading into old age（從此到老都能繼續閱讀），所以對這項新發明「讚不絕口」；句首 Still（儘管如此）承接前一句「很少一般人買得起」。credit 意思相近，但英文不說 full of credit for。
evidence: Still, scholars and monks, who could now keep reading into old age, were full of [[5]] for the new invention.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward（形容詞，不方便的、不好用的；也常指「尷尬的」）詞性不合：空格在 were full of 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: full of device 不通（device 是可數名詞，也不是對新發明的態度）；device 屬於第 10 格。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 were full of 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 were full of 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.F: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 were full of 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: demand 是名詞，但 full of demand for 不是英文說法；學者和修士能繼續閱讀，說的是他們對發明的態度，不是市場需求。demand 屬於第 6 格。
option_notes_zh.H: suit 當名詞是「西裝」，full of suit for 不通；suit 在本文是第 9 格的動詞。
option_notes_zh.I: credit 和 praise 意思相近，但只說 take credit for，不說 full of credit for；credit 屬於第 3 格。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive（形容詞，昂貴的）詞性不合：空格在 were full of 之後、for 之前，需要名詞。

5.strategy_zh: be full of ___ for 要名詞；能到老都繼續讀書，學者和修士對眼鏡當然是「讚美」。
hints: were full of ___ for：需要名詞。
學者和修士到老都能繼續讀書，他們對這項新發明有什麼反應？
be full of ___ for＝對……讚不絕口。

6.explanation_zh: the ___ for glasses rose sharply 需要名詞當主詞；the demand for（對……的需求）是固定搭配，常和 rose sharply（急遽上升）連用。印刷術讓書本大量普及，讀書的人變多，對眼鏡的「需求」也急遽上升；and 後面 workshops began producing them in large numbers（作坊開始大量生產）正是需求增加的結果。
evidence: After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[6]] for glasses rose sharply, and workshops began producing them in large numbers.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward（形容詞，不方便的、不好用的；也常指「尷尬的」）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞當主詞。
option_notes_zh.B: the device for glasses rose sharply 不通；device 屬於第 10 格。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞當主詞。
option_notes_zh.D: praise 是名詞，但 rose sharply（急遽上升）描述的是數量；and 後面說作坊開始大量生產，說的是買眼鏡的人變多，不是讚美。praise 屬於第 5 格 full of praise for。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞當主詞。
option_notes_zh.F: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞當主詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit 當名詞是「西裝」，the suit for glasses rose 不通；suit 在本文是第 9 格的動詞。
option_notes_zh.I: the credit for glasses rose sharply（眼鏡的功勞急遽上升）不通；credit 屬於第 3 格。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive（形容詞，昂貴的）詞性不合：空格在 the 之後、for glasses 之前，需要名詞當主詞。

6.strategy_zh: 冠詞與 for 之間要名詞；書本普及 → 讀者變多 → 作坊大量生產，中間缺的是「需求」。
hints: the ___ for glasses：需要名詞，當句子主詞。
書本變多、讀書的人增加，作坊又開始大量生產，什麼東西 rose sharply？
答案和 supply（供應）意思相對。

7.explanation_zh: were ___ to wear 需要形容詞（形容詞＋to V）。冒號後說明原因：鏡框 pinched the nose and slipped off at the slightest movement（會夾鼻子、稍微一動就滑落），所以早期的鏡框戴起來很「不方便」。awkward 最常見的意思是「尷尬的」，這裡用的是「（東西）不好用、不方便的」。
evidence: Early frames, however, were [[7]] to wear: they pinched the nose and slipped off at the slightest movement.

option_notes_zh.B: device（名詞，裝置、器材）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.D: praise（名詞，讚美、稱讚（也可當動詞））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed 是形容詞，但主詞是 frames（鏡框），物品不會「感到羞愧」；ashamed 屬於第 8 格 were ashamed of。
option_notes_zh.F: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.G: demand（名詞，需求（也可當動詞「要求」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit（動詞，適合（也可當名詞「西裝」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.I: credit（名詞，功勞、讚揚；take credit for＝居功）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to wear 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive 是形容詞，但冒號後說的是夾鼻子、容易滑落，和價錢無關，也不說 expensive to wear；expensive 屬於第 4 格。

7.strategy_zh: 形容詞＋to V；冒號後的說明（夾鼻、滑落）就是答案的內容，再用主詞是物品排除 ashamed。
hints: were ___ to wear：需要形容詞。
冒號後說鏡框會夾鼻子、容易滑落，戴起來感覺如何？
答案常譯「尷尬的」，這裡指「不方便的」。

8.explanation_zh: were ___ of wearing them 需要能接 of 的形容詞；be ashamed of（以……為恥、羞於……）是固定搭配。眼鏡被視為 a sign of weakness or old age（軟弱或衰老的象徵），所以許多人「羞於」在公開場合戴眼鏡。
evidence: For centuries, glasses were also seen as a sign of weakness or old age, and many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward 是形容詞，但不和 of 搭配（awkward of wearing 不通）；awkward 屬於第 7 格 awkward to wear。
option_notes_zh.B: device（名詞，裝置、器材）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify（動詞，放大）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.D: praise（名詞，讚美、稱讚（也可當動詞））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.F: give up（片語動詞，放棄）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.G: demand（名詞，需求（也可當動詞「要求」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.H: suit（動詞，適合（也可當名詞「西裝」））詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.I: credit（名詞，功勞、讚揚；take credit for＝居功）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、of 之前，需要能接 of 的形容詞。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive 是形容詞，但主詞是 many people，「人很昂貴」不通，expensive 也不接 of；expensive 屬於第 4 格。

8.strategy_zh: 看介系詞 of 決定形容詞：be ashamed of；再用「軟弱、衰老的象徵」確認是羞恥的感受。
hints: were ___ of：需要能接 of 的形容詞。
眼鏡被當成軟弱、衰老的象徵，戴眼鏡的人會有什麼感受？
be ___ of＝以……為恥。

9.explanation_zh: frames that ___ their face and personality 中，that 代替複數的 frames，空格要用現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形）。suit 當動詞是「適合」：眼鏡有各式各樣的造型和顏色（all kinds of shapes and colors），所以人們挑選「適合」自己臉型和個性的鏡框。
evidence: Glasses now come in all kinds of shapes and colors, and many people choose frames that [[9]] their face and personality.

option_notes_zh.A: awkward（形容詞，不方便的、不好用的；也常指「尷尬的」）詞性不合：空格在關係代名詞 that（先行詞 frames）之後，需要現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形），受詞是 their face and personality。
option_notes_zh.B: device（名詞，裝置、器材）詞性不合：空格在關係代名詞 that（先行詞 frames）之後，需要現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形），受詞是 their face and personality。
option_notes_zh.C: magnify 是原形動詞，但 frames that magnify their face（放大臉的鏡框）不合「挑選喜歡的造型和顏色」的語境；magnify 屬於第 2 格。
option_notes_zh.D: praise 也可當動詞，但 frames that praise their face（讚美臉的鏡框）不通；praise 在本文是第 5 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.E: ashamed（形容詞，感到羞愧的；be ashamed of＝以……為恥）詞性不合：空格在關係代名詞 that（先行詞 frames）之後，需要現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形），受詞是 their face and personality。
option_notes_zh.F: give up their face and personality（放棄臉型和個性）不通；give up 屬於第 1 格。
option_notes_zh.G: demand 也可當動詞，但 frames that demand their face 不通；demand 在本文是第 6 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.I: credit 也可當動詞，但 frames that credit their face 不通；credit 在本文是第 3 格的名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: expensive（形容詞，昂貴的）詞性不合：空格在關係代名詞 that（先行詞 frames）之後，需要現在式的及物動詞（複數主詞用原形），受詞是 their face and personality。

9.strategy_zh: that 指複數的 frames，空格要現在式動詞；挑鏡框的標準是「適合」自己。
hints: frames that ___ their face：that 指 frames，空格要用現在式的動詞。
眼鏡有各種造型和顏色，人們會挑什麼樣的鏡框？
suit 除了「西裝」，當動詞是「適合」。

translation_zh.text:
今天，數百萬人每天早上不假思索地戴上眼鏡。然而在歷史上大部分的時間裡，視力隨年紀退化的人只能忍受一個模糊的世界。隨著閱讀和縫紉一年比一年困難，許多技術工人遠比自己希望的更早就被迫放棄手藝。
有些讀者會把一片磨亮的水晶放在書頁上來放大字母，讓字看起來更大。真正的眼鏡在十三世紀末出現在義大利北部，但沒有人能把發明眼鏡的功勞歸給自己，因為製作者的名字從未被記錄下來。這些早期的眼鏡沒有鏡腳，使用者必須用手拿著，或把它們架在鼻子上。由於每片鏡片都是手工磨製，眼鏡起初非常昂貴，很少一般人買得起。儘管如此，學者和修士從此到老都能繼續讀書，對這項新發明讚不絕口。
十五世紀中葉印刷術讓書本普及之後，對眼鏡的需求急遽上升，作坊也開始大量生產。給看不清楚遠處物體的人使用的鏡片則是後來才出現。不過，早期的鏡框戴起來很不方便：會夾鼻子，稍微一動就滑落。直到十八世紀，架在耳朵上的鏡腳才變得普遍，配戴者從此不必再用手扶著眼鏡。
幾百年來，眼鏡也被視為軟弱或衰老的象徵，許多人都羞於在公開場合戴眼鏡。如今，人們的看法已完全改變。眼鏡有各式各樣的造型和顏色，許多人會挑選適合自己臉型和個性的鏡框。有些人甚至只因為喜歡那種造型就戴上平光眼鏡，把醫療器材變成了時尚配件。

evidence: As reading and sewing grew harder each year, many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.
1.explanation_zh: 空格後接受詞 their trades，且前文說視力退化使閱讀、縫紉愈來愈難，工匠被迫提早「放棄」本業，用動詞片語 give up。

evidence: Some readers laid a piece of polished crystal on the page to [[2]] the letters, making them look bigger.
2.explanation_zh: to 後需原形動詞；後面 making them look bigger 說明水晶讓字變大，故為 magnify（放大）。

evidence: The first true eyeglasses appeared in northern Italy in the late 1200s, yet no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded.
3.explanation_zh: take credit for 為固定搭配「因…而獲得功勞」；後句說發明者姓名沒有留下紀錄，所以沒有人能居功。

evidence: Because every lens was shaped by hand, glasses were so [[4]] at first that few ordinary people could afford them.
4.explanation_zh: so…that 句型，結果是一般人買不起（few ordinary people could afford them），且鏡片都是手工磨製，故為 expensive。

evidence: Still, scholars and monks, who could now keep reading into old age, were full of [[5]] for the new invention.
5.explanation_zh: be full of praise for 為「對…讚不絕口」；學者與修士因能讀書到老而稱讚這項發明。

evidence: After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[6]] for glasses rose sharply, and workshops began producing them in large numbers.
6.explanation_zh: 印刷術讓書本普及後，眼鏡的「需求」大增，工坊開始大量生產；the demand for 為固定搭配。

evidence: Early frames, however, were [[7]] to wear: they pinched the nose and slipped off at the slightest movement.
7.explanation_zh: 冒號後說明鏡框會夾鼻子、稍動就滑落，表示戴起來「不舒服、彆扭」，故為 awkward。

evidence: For centuries, glasses were also seen as a sign of weakness or old age, and many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public.
8.explanation_zh: be ashamed of 為「以…為恥」；前半句說眼鏡被視為虛弱或年老的象徵，所以人們不好意思在公開場合戴。

evidence: Glasses now come in all kinds of shapes and colors, and many people choose frames that [[9]] their face and personality.
9.explanation_zh: 關係子句 that 後需動詞；選擇「適合」自己臉型與個性的鏡框，suit 符合語意。

evidence: Some even wear glasses with plain lenses just because they like the look, turning a medical [[10]] into a fashion accessory.
10.explanation_zh: medical 後需名詞，眼鏡本是醫療「器具」，如今變成時尚配件，故為 device。

evidence: As reading and sewing grew harder each year, many skilled workers were forced to [[1]] their trades long before they wished to.
1.explanation_zh: forced to 後接原形動詞，give up their trades（放棄行業）合理。

evidence: Some readers laid a piece of polished crystal on the page to [[2]] the letters, making them look bigger.
2.explanation_zh: to 後接原形動詞，且 making them look bigger 說明是放大字母 magnify。

evidence: The first true eyeglasses appeared in northern Italy in the late 1200s, yet no one can take [[3]] for inventing them, because the maker’s name was never recorded.
3.explanation_zh: take credit for inventing（居功）是慣用語，且發明者名字未被記錄。

evidence: Because every lens was shaped by hand, glasses were so [[4]] at first that few ordinary people could afford them.
4.explanation_zh: so ... that few ordinary people could afford them，表示價格昂貴。

evidence: Still, scholars and monks, who could now keep reading into old age, were full of [[5]] for the new invention.
5.explanation_zh: full of praise for the new invention（滿是讚美），學者與僧侶受惠。

evidence: After the printing press made books far more common in the mid-1400s, the [[6]] for glasses rose sharply, and workshops began producing them in large numbers.
6.explanation_zh: 書變多後對眼鏡的需求上升，工坊才大量生產。

evidence: Early frames, however, were [[7]] to wear: they pinched the nose and slipped off at the slightest movement.
7.explanation_zh: were awkward to wear 後面說夾鼻又易滑落，指戴起來不舒服不方便。

evidence: For centuries, glasses were also seen as a sign of weakness or old age, and many people were [[8]] of wearing them in public.
8.explanation_zh: ashamed of wearing them in public，因眼鏡被視為弱點或老態的象徵。

evidence: Glasses now come in all kinds of shapes and colors, and many people choose frames that [[9]] their face and personality.
9.explanation_zh: frames that suit their face and personality（適合臉型與個性）。
